Governance shock dominated the day: Casey Newton amplified a WSJ report that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang — the batch's highest-scored and most consequential story, though still unconfirmed.

entry.title: @TimDarcet @gabriberton The P in JEPA stands for predictive. The main distinction is not between JEA...
entry.summary: LeCun continues yesterday's Social thread, adding formal loss formulations and the history of anti-collapse methods. Yann LeCun (@ylecun) responds to a discussion by clarifying the taxonomy of joint-embedding architectures: the P in JEPA stands for predictive, and the fundamental distinction is not between JEA and JEPA but between joint-embedding approaches (predictive or not) and generative architectures. He lays out formal loss formulations: generative models predict y from x with a divergence loss between target and prediction, while JEA encodes both x and y and minimizes representation divergence with an anti-collapse regularizer R, useful when neither view has a privileged direction (e.g., two views of the same scene). He adds historical depth, citing Becker and Hinton's 1989 information-maximization anti-collapse model and noting Schmidhuber's early related work, and notes that whether a predictor is needed depends on the task.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 06, 2026
entry.summary:
Breaking capability and security news dominated discussions. OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, a security-research model reportedly already defending Linux kernel code, announced alongside a major strategic partnership with JPMorganChase.

  • Thomas Wolf released a free ~70,000-word MoE Training Handbook based on 800k GPU hours of experiments, arguing dense open models are 'basically over'
  • METR estimates Anthropic is improving capabilities at ~2× the historical rate, possibly 3×, igniting recursive self-improvement debate; METR also criticized Anthropic for redacting most of its public assessment
  • Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small jumped 18 points to 31 on the Artificial Analysis index; Tencent's Hy4 scored 35, tying Grok 4.7
  • Perplexity launched Teammates proactive work agents, with ~10,000 already active internally — roughly 20× its human headcount
  • Jim Fan introduced VFlash parallel vision decoding for physical AI, while Soumith Chintala shared unusually transparent training details for a small v2 model
  • Gary Marcus went viral declaring a market 'day of reckoning' amid double-digit AI stock losses, echoing voter backlash against new data centers
  • Evaluation distrust ran as a strong undercurrent: swyx argued independent evaluators must rebuild lab benchmarks, and Hamel Husain urged practitioners to run private evals

Community sentiment split between capability optimism — security agents, MoE scale, real agent adoption — and skepticism over benchmark integrity, lab transparency, and market sustainability.
